title: What affects a canapé catering quote in Dubai?
body_markdown:
A canapé catering quote in Dubai depends on the menu, portions per guest, service duration, staffing, equipment and venue arrangements. The main canapé catering quote factors are not just the ingredients: preparation, transport, serving and clearing also need a defined scope. Compare proposals against the same brief, and ask what sits outside the quoted total before choosing.


**TL;DR**

- Compare canapé catering quote factors against the same guest count, menu, service window and venue brief.
- Food delivery and staffed canapé service have different responsibilities; confirm who sets up, serves and clears.
- myCHEF provides private chefs and event catering for households and businesses in Dubai.
- Ask for portions per guest, dietary arrangements, equipment and exclusions in writing before accepting a proposal.


## What affects a canapé catering quote in Dubai?

**A useful quote defines both the food and the work required to serve it.** A menu description alone does not tell you how much food each guest receives, whether someone passes trays, or who clears the venue afterwards.

Start by separating the following elements. For a closer look at the practical responsibilities, read the guide to [serving staff and catering cleanup](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/can-catering-companies-in-dubai-provide-serving-staff-and-cleanup).

| Quote element | What to ask the caterer | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| Menu | Which individual canapés are included? | Ingredients and preparation methods define the food being supplied. |
| Portions | How many pieces does each guest receive? | Menu variety is not the same as food quantity. |
| Service | Is the food delivered, displayed or passed by staff? | Each format leaves different tasks with your host or venue team. |
| Staffing | Which roles are included, and for what hours? | Preparation, service and clearing need a clear division of responsibility. |
| Equipment | Are trays, serviceware and preparation equipment included? | A food proposal does not automatically cover an event setup. |
| Logistics | What access, delivery and collection arrangements apply? | The caterer needs a workable route from arrival to service. |

Ask for a total tied to a specific version of your brief. If the guest count, menu or service window changes, request a revised proposal rather than assuming the original scope still applies.

## Why the scope matters more than the headline figure

A canapé reception before dinner has a different purpose from an evening where canapés are the only food. Tell the caterer which event you are planning before discussing the menu.

The same applies to the host’s role. If you want to greet guests throughout the evening, a delivery-only proposal leaves you with work that a staffed proposal assigns to someone else. Neither format is inherently better; the right choice depends on the responsibilities you want to keep.

**Compare the complete event scope, not just the food description.** Otherwise, you risk choosing between proposals that solve different problems.

## Which canapé service format suits your event?

Choose the service format before refining individual dishes. It determines how guests receive food, where equipment goes and who manages the room.

The following comparison describes formats to discuss with a caterer, not confirmed myCHEF packages or inclusions.

| Format | Best for | Main advantage | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivered canapés | Hosts with an agreed serving arrangement | Separates food preparation from on-site hosting | You must assign presentation, replenishment and clearing unless agreed otherwise. |
| Staffed tray service | Receptions where guests mingle | Servers take food around the room | Requires defined staffing hours and a preparation or staging area. |
| Staffed canapé display | Events with a designated food area | Gives guests a clear place to choose food | Requires space and an agreed replenishment plan. |

### Delivered canapés: best for hosts managing service

Choose delivery when you or the venue team can take responsibility for the food after handover. Ask how each item should be presented and whether anything needs finishing before guests arrive.

Confirm delivery timing, packaging and collection arrangements. Do not treat delivery as staffed catering unless the proposal explicitly includes those duties.

### Staffed tray service: best for mingling receptions

Choose tray service when you want food to circulate while guests talk. Ask the caterer to explain how trays will move between the staging area and the guest space.

Clarify who replenishes trays, answers ingredient questions and removes used serviceware. A chef and a server perform different jobs; the proposal should identify the roles your event needs.

### Staffed canapé display: best for a fixed serving area

Choose a display when your venue has a suitable place for guests to collect food. Confirm who supplies the surface, sets it up and keeps it replenished.

The trade-off is space. Check that the display does not obstruct entrances, seating or the route between the kitchen and guest area.

## Why canapé catering quotes vary

These factors explain the differences you should ask a caterer to identify. They are briefing points, not standard surcharges or promised inclusions.

- **Menu:** Specify the dishes rather than requesting only a cuisine or theme. Ask which items need individual assembly or on-site finishing.
- **Portions:** State whether canapés accompany another meal or provide the event’s main food. Request the planned quantity per guest.
- **Staffing:** Define preparation, tray service, replenishment and clearing responsibilities. Ask for the working hours attached to each role.
- **Venue:** Describe kitchen access, preparation space, loading arrangements and the route to the event area. Include any venue restrictions you have confirmed.
- **Timing:** Share arrival, setup, guest arrival, food service and collection times. Distinguish the guest-facing event from the crew’s working window.
- **Dietary requirements:** Give the caterer specific requirements and ask how suitable items will be prepared, identified and served.


![Six briefing factors connected to the scope of a canapé catering quote](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/ee299e54-e3e5-47f6-bd4f-2112fcb6e31a/body-754b9d08c26be015b53424ca16ec2a2d.jpg)

*Define these details before comparing proposals.*


A useful proposal connects these details rather than listing them in isolation. For example, food that needs finishing on site also needs an agreed preparation area and someone responsible for that work. Ask the caterer to explain the relationship, not simply add an unexplained line item.

## How should you brief the menu and portions?

Start with the role of the food. Is it a welcome reception, a gathering between meals, or the main food offering for the evening? Then describe the guests, service style and dietary requirements.

Ask for the proposed canapé selection alongside the quantity per guest. A long list of dishes does not establish whether everyone receives each item or chooses from a shared allocation.

### Ask how the selection will be distributed

Request a breakdown that distinguishes the overall quantity from the mix of dishes. If particular items are intended for guests with dietary requirements, clarify how those portions will reach them.

This also helps you assess substitutions. A replacement should have an agreed role in the menu, rather than leaving you uncertain about what a guest can eat.

### Keep a sample menu clearly illustrative

An illustrative brief might request a mixture of vegetable-led bites, savoury pastries and more substantial items, with a separately agreed dietary selection. That describes a direction for discussion; it is not a confirmed menu or a recommendation for every event.

Ask the caterer to propose dishes suited to your venue and service format. **Choose food that works with the serving arrangements, not just food that reads well on a menu.**

## What should the quote include and exclude?

Request an inclusion list you can check against the event plan. Avoid relying on a broad description such as complete catering without an explanation of the tasks and equipment covered.

Use this checklist when reviewing the proposal:

- **Food:** Named menu items, quantities and agreed substitutions.
- **Preparation:** Where food is prepared and what finishing happens at the venue.
- **People:** Chef, serving and coordination responsibilities, where required.
- **Serviceware:** Trays, plates, napkins, utensils and any presentation pieces.
- **Venue setup:** Preparation surfaces, serving furniture and equipment responsibilities.
- **Transport:** Delivery, unloading, collection and access arrangements.
- **Close-down:** Clearing, washing up, waste handling and equipment removal.
- **Terms:** Applicable taxes, payment conditions, amendment terms and exclusions.

Beverages, glassware, furniture and venue charges also need an explicit answer if they form part of your plans. Do not assume the food proposal covers them.

When a requirement is excluded, decide who will supply it before confirming the event. An exclusion is manageable when responsibility is clear; an unassigned task becomes the host’s problem on the day.

## What venue details should you share in Dubai?

Give the caterer the exact location and the practical access information supplied by your building or venue. For an apartment or office, ask about loading access, lift use and any supplier arrival procedures.

For a villa, explain where preparation and service will happen. Share the available kitchen facilities rather than assuming the caterer can use every appliance or surface.

If you are planning an outdoor reception, identify the intended food area and discuss an alternative arrangement with the venue and caterer. Keep this conversation specific to the menu and setup rather than assuming an indoor plan transfers outside unchanged.

Photographs of the preparation area and access route can make the brief clearer. Use them to show the working space, not just the guest-facing setting.

## How do you compare proposals fairly?

Send each caterer the same brief and ask for responses against the same scope. Keep a record of revisions so that a menu change does not get confused with a change in staffing or service.

1. **Fix the event brief.** Use the same date, location, guest count and service window.
2. **Match the food quantity.** Compare portions and menu composition, not dish names alone.
3. **Match the responsibilities.** Identify who prepares, serves, replenishes and clears.
4. **Check the exclusions.** Resolve equipment, transport and venue responsibilities.
5. **Confirm the final version.** Obtain a written proposal reflecting the choices you have agreed.

If you need to reduce the scope, ask the caterer to explain the practical consequence of each change. Simplifying the menu is a different decision from removing serving staff or shortening service.

## FAQ


**What are the main canapé catering quote factors in Dubai?**

The main canapé catering quote factors are menu selection, portions per guest, staffing, service duration, equipment and venue logistics. Ask for a written scope that separates food from service and identifies exclusions.

**How much does canapé catering cost per person in Dubai?**

Request a current quote based on your event brief rather than relying on a universal per-person figure. Compare the menu, portions, staffing, equipment and service window included in each proposal.

**Does a canapé catering quote include serving staff?**

A canapé catering quote includes serving staff only when the proposal explicitly lists them. Confirm their duties and working hours, including setup and clearing where required.

**How many canapés should I order per guest?**

Ask the caterer to recommend portions based on whether canapés accompany a meal or provide the main food. Confirm both the quantity per guest and how the selection will be distributed.

**Is delivery-only canapé catering suitable for a home party?**

Delivery-only canapé catering suits a home party when you have assigned presentation, serving, replenishment and clearing. Discuss any finishing requirements before choosing this format.

**Can I request canapés for guests with dietary requirements?**

Include each dietary requirement in the initial brief and ask the caterer to confirm what can be accommodated. For allergies, discuss ingredients, preparation and cross-contact handling before agreeing the menu.

**What should I send when asking myCHEF for a canapé quote?**

Send myCHEF your event date, location, guest count and required service. Add the food service window, dietary requirements and venue access details so the enquiry has a clear scope.

## Before you request your quote

Ask one final question: **who owns each task after the food arrives?** Delivery, presentation, replenishment and clearing are separate responsibilities. Naming the person responsible for each makes the proposal easier to assess and the event easier to host.

Send your date, Dubai location, guest count and required canapé service to myCHEF. Include whether the food accompanies another meal, your dietary requirements and the venue’s preparation facilities, so your enquiry starts with the details needed for a tailored quote.
